name: Cerro Blanco – Mita
summary: A moderate-to-high-temperature system discovered in 1997 alongside the Cerro Blanco epithermal gold deposit in Jutiapa, near the El Salvador border. Slimhole exploration wells confirmed a deep reservoir up to ~218°C, structurally controlled by east-west faulting east/northeast of the gold deposit and defined by a resistivity dome identified in MT geophysics. No surface steam discharge; cooling is largely conductive, with chloride geochemistry pointing to a deep magmatic source.
